\[
H(x,y) = I(x,y) - (G_{\sigma} \star I)(x,y),
\qquad
\sigma = 2
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(H\): High-pass result, signed
- \(G_{\sigma}\): Normalized Gaussian kernel with radius floor(3 sigma + 0.5)
- \(\star\): Correlation
- \(\sigma\): Standard deviation of the Gaussian in pixels

The Gaussian blur keeps the coarse picture. What is left after subtracting it from the image is the fine detail H, a signed value that is 0 in flat areas. The output mapping turns it into a visible image. The default adds 128, so flat areas are middle gray.
